textbookText: A. Tick the correct alternative. 1. Which type of adaptation is shown by fishes? a. primary aquatic b. secondary aquatic c. burrowing d. scansorial 2. Swim bladder is the specialized organ that helps certain aquatic animals to maintain buoyancy in water which is crucial to remain floating in water effortlessly. In which of the following animals’ swim bladder is primarily found? a. aquatic mammals such as whale and dolphin b. bony fishes that live in freshwater c. cartilaginous fishes which live in marine water d. aquatic Reptiles like sea turtle, crocodiles, water snake 3. Sensory organs present in the lateral line system in fishes are……. a. neurons b. neuromasts c. chromatophores d. neuroglia 4. Which of the following statement is true for whale? a. whale repires by gills b. whale respires by moist skin c. whale is amphibious d. whale respires by Lungs 5. Cursorial adaptation is the evolutionary modification found in animals, adapted for running efficiently on the ground. Such adaptation helps in high speed locomotion over terrestrial habitat. Which of the following group of animal known for exhibiting cursorial adaptation? a. cheetah, frog pigeon, horse b. lion, whale, fish, bat c. cheetah, tiger, lion horse d. monkey, lion, frog pigeon 6. Which of the following type of locomotion is found in animals of cat family? a. unguligrade b. digitigrade c. plantigrade d. crawling 7. Identify the mode of locomotion is found in the given animal.

a. digitigrade b. unguligrade c. plantigrade d. swimming 8. An animal was seen on the land, with compact, spindle shaped body and conical snout. Its forelimbs are short strong with sharp claws with shovel like palms. Based on these characteristics, what would be the adaptation of this animal? a. arboreal- living in tree b. aquatic – swimming in water c. volant- flying in air d. fossorial – burrowing 9. Which of the following is not true for Fossorial adaptation? a. they live underground b. they have shovel like palm with clawed digits c. the have small, stout body with pointed snout d. they live mostly in trees 10. Those animals which are adapted for climbing called……… a. cursorial animal b. scansorial animal c. aquatic animal d. burrowing animal 11. Saumyata saw a lizard climbing the wall of her house. Then she tried to catch it but its tail was suddenly broken off but the lizard continued to climb up. After sharing about this event to her teacher. She learned about the ability of lizard to regenerates its tail. What is this phenomenon called? a. metamorphosis b. autotomy c. vasectomy d. moulting 12. Which type of adaptation is shown by Gibbon………. a. arboreal b. cursorial c. fossorial d. aquatic 13. Bat possesses unique anatomical features which enable them to sustain flight and navigate through air. Considering the adaptation which of the following organ is primarily responsible for sustaining flight? a. pneumatic bones with fur on their body b. modified forelimbs with elongated finger connected by wing membrane

c. webbed feet that provides propulsion through air d. wings with feather 14. The mechanism of gripping objects like tree branch, wire, rope etc. by their hind limbs without any risk of falling down is……. a. flight b. perching c. gliding d. resting 15. In flying fish, which of the following fins are modified as patagia? a. anal fin b. pelvic fin c. caudal d. pectoral fin B. Answer the following questions: 1. What do you mean by secondary aquatic adaptation? Enlist the various adaptational features of secondary aquatic animals with examples. 2. Rahu is the freshwater animal. What type of adaptation and morphological features are found in its body? 3. What are arboreal animals? How are they suited to survive in their habitat? 4. Enlist the adaptational features of animals showing cursorial adaptation. 5. Compare and contrast primary aquatic animals and secondary aquatic animals. 6. Compare and contrast volant animals with cursorial animals. 7. Which type of adaptation is found in bat and birds? How are they are modified for flying in air? 8. What do you mean by gliding adaptation? Write any four examples of animal showing gliding adaptation and also mention their adaptational features. 9.
